usage.title:
AnsibleForms installer.
It installs, upgrades and maintains AnsibleForms.
usage.install: install AnsibleForms, as a controller or a Runner (the default)
usage.upgrade: upgrade to a newer version, showing its release notes first
usage.status: show the installation and its containers or pods
usage.releaseNotes: show the release notes of a version
usage.flags:
Flags. Each one answers a question.
--yes answers the remaining questions with their defaults.
check.name: Only lowercase letters, digits and -
check.url: An address starting with http:// or https://
install.role: What do you want to install?
install.roleController: A controller: AnsibleForms, its database and a Runner
install.roleRunner: A Runner: an RTE for an AnsibleForms installed elsewhere
install.noRuntime:
Neither Docker nor Podman is installed on this server.
The installer can install one of them.
install.confirmRuntime:
Install {runtime} now?

Install Docker or Podman, then run the installer again.

install.adminPassword: Password for the first admin (leave empty to generate one)

These versions contain breaking changes or removals.
Have you read them, and do you want to continue?
upgrade.rollback:
Roll back to the previous version?

upgrade.rollbackFailed: The rollback failed. The backup is kept for a manual restore
upgrade.rolledBack: Rolled back to the previous version.
notes.deprecated: Deprecated (to be removed in a later major version)
uninstall.purge: Also delete its data (database, forms, playbooks, logs)?
uninstall.typeName: Type the name {name} to delete it along with its data
uninstall.nameMismatch: The name does not match the instance. Nothing was removed.
install.roleHelp:
This installs AnsibleForms {version}.
A controller is the complete application.
A Runner only runs playbooks for a controller.
install.roleControllerHint:
The web interface, its database and its own Runner.
On this server or on Kubernetes.
Choose this for a first installation.
install.roleRunnerHint:
It runs the playbooks of an AnsibleForms installed elsewhere.
For example in another network, a DMZ or another datacenter.
It talks to AnsibleForms over a single WebSocket.
install.modeKubernetesHint:
The Helm chart, on the cluster that kubectl reaches.
It is served behind an ingress.
install.runtimeHelp:
Docker and Podman are both installed on this server.
Choose the one that runs AnsibleForms.
runtime.dockerHint:
Docker Engine with its compose plugin.
The containers restart together with Docker.
runtime.podmanHint:
Podman, rootless or as root.
A systemd unit starts the containers at boot.
runtime.dockerInstallHint:
Installed with Docker's official script (get.docker.com).
The compose plugin is included.
runtime.podmanInstallHint:
Installed from this distribution's packages.
podman-compose is included.
install.dirHelp:
The compose file and its .env with the secrets are stored here.
So is all the data: database, forms, playbooks and logs.
install.nameHelp:
Its containers are named after it: af_app, af_db, af_rte.
Different names let several instances share one server.
install.portHelp: The port the web interface listens on.
runner.portHelp:
Outbound, only the health checks listen on this port.
They are reachable from this server only.
Inbound, AnsibleForms connects to the Runner on this port.
runner.addressHelp:
The address AnsibleForms uses to reach this server.
An inbound Runner receives the connection from AnsibleForms.
install.tlsHelp:
How browsers connect to it.
HTTPS is strongly recommended: logins and secrets go through it.
install.tlsSelfHint:
A certificate created here for this server's names.
It is valid for ten years.
Browsers ask you to accept it once.
install.tlsOwnHint:
Your own certificate and key, in PEM format.
From your CA, or from Let's Encrypt.
install.tlsOffHint:
Plain HTTP on the port.
For a reverse proxy in front that handles HTTPS.
For example nginx, Traefik or a load balancer.
install.adminPasswordHelp:
The password of the admin user, the first account.
Leave it empty to generate a strong one.
It is shown at the end.
review.name: Name
runner.appUrlHelp:
The address of the AnsibleForms this Runner works for.
The same address people open in a browser.
runner.modeHelp:
Both modes use a single WebSocket.
Only the side that opens the connection differs.
runner.modeOutboundHint:
The Runner opens the connection to AnsibleForms and keeps it open.
Only traffic from this server to AnsibleForms, on its port.
Nothing from outside reaches this server.
For a DMZ, NAT, or a zone that allows no incoming connections.
runner.modeInboundHint:
AnsibleForms opens the connection to the Runner.
It connects to this server's address and port.
For networks where the central side opens every connection.
upgrade.notesHelp:
What changes from {from} to {to}.
Breaking changes and removals are listed first.
upgrade.backupHelp:
The database is backed up first.
If the new version does not respond, you can roll back.
install.notesHelp:
Read this before you install.
Breaking changes, removals and deprecations are listed first.
install.notesUnavailable:
The release notes for {version} could not be loaded.
They are on https://github.com/ansibleforms/ansibleforms/releases
install.runtimeHelpOne:
{runtime} is installed on this server.
The installer can also install {other} instead.
install.modeKubernetesMissing: Kubernetes (requires kubectl, helm and a reachable cluster)
install.runtimeHelpKube:
A Kubernetes cluster is reachable too.
The Helm chart can install AnsibleForms there.
language.title: Which language should the installer use?
language.help:
The default comes from this server's locale.
The installer can also be started with --lang.
install.modeKubernetesRunner: Kubernetes (a Runner there is installed with the Helm chart)
install.modeNative: Directly on this server, no containers
install.modeNative_root: Directly on this server (needs root: run the installer with sudo)
install.modeNative_unsupported: Directly on this server (not supported on this Linux)
install.modeNativeHint:
Node.js, MariaDB and Ansible are installed on this server.
AnsibleForms and its Runner run as systemd services.
For servers where containers are not allowed.
install.modeNativeRunnerHint:
Node.js, Python and Ansible are installed on this server.
The Runner runs as a systemd service.
For servers where containers are not allowed.
install.nameNative: Instance name (its services and system user)
install.nameHelpNative:
Its systemd services and its system user are named after it.
Different names let several instances share one server.
install.dirHelpNative:
AnsibleForms, Node.js, Python and the settings go here.
So does all the data: forms, playbooks and logs.
The database itself is kept by MariaDB.
native.cannot_root:
Installing directly on this server needs root.
Run the installer with sudo.
native.cannot_unsupported:
Installing directly on this server is not supported on this Linux.
Use Docker or Podman instead.
native.exists:
A service named {name} already exists.
Choose another instance name.
native.python: Installing Python {version} and Ansible (a few minutes)
native.sshpassMissing:
sshpass could not be installed.
Playbooks cannot sign in with SSH passwords until it is.
native.notReady:
The service {unit} did not start.
See its log: journalctl -u {unit}
native.noBundle:
AnsibleForms {version} has no bundle for this server.
Installing without containers needs AnsibleForms 7.3.0 or later.
native.data: Downloading the starting forms, playbooks and settings
detect.looking: Looking for an AnsibleForms already on this server
detect.found: AnsibleForms is already on this server, but this installer does not manage it yet:
detect.foundHelp:
Take it over to upgrade it from here.
A second installation beside it could clash on ports, the database or folders.
detect.foundHelpNone:
The installer cannot upgrade it: see why above.
A second installation beside it could clash on ports, the database or folders.
detect.choose: What do you want to do?
detect.adoptHint:
The installer remembers where it is and how it runs, then upgrades it.
It backs up the database first and can roll back.
detect.alongside: Install a new AnsibleForms beside it anyway
detect.alongsideHint:
A separate installation, with its own folder, ports and database.
The one found is left as it is.
detect.alongsideHelp:
A second AnsibleForms needs its own ports, folder and database.
The installer refuses a folder or container names in use, but it cannot check everything.
detect.alongsideConfirm: Install a second AnsibleForms on this server?
detect.unattended:
AnsibleForms is already on this server and the installer does not manage it.
Run the installer without --yes to choose what to do.
When only one is found, ansibleforms-installer upgrade --yes takes it over and upgrades it.
detect.cannotAdopt: AnsibleForms was found on this server, but the installer cannot upgrade it: see why above.
detect.adoptReview: The installer will remember this installation in {file}:
detect.adoptCompose:
The upgrade backs up the database, docker-compose.yml and .env first.
It then replaces docker-compose.yml with the one of the ansibleforms/docker repository.
The .env and the data folder are kept as they are.
detect.adoptRunner:
The upgrade rewrites docker-compose.yml for the new RTE image.
The .env and the data folder are kept as they are.
detect.adoptKube:
The release's current values are saved next to installer.json.
The upgrades apply them again, with the chart of the new version.
detect.adoptNative:
The upgrade puts the new release in releases/ and moves the current link.
The settings and the data folder are kept as they are.
detect.adopted: The installer now manages this installation ({file}).
detect.unmanagedTitle: On this server, not managed by the installer:
detect.statusAdopt: Run ansibleforms-installer upgrade to take it over and upgrade it.
detect.why_notCompose:
Its containers were not started with Docker Compose.
Upgrade them by hand, the way they were started.
detect.why_noComposeFile:
The installer cannot read docker-compose.yml and .env in {dir}.
Run the installer as root or as the folder's owner.
detect.why_notRepoLayout:
Its compose file does not follow the ansibleforms/docker repository.
That is the services mysqldb, app and rte, in containers <name>_db, _app and _rte.
Upgrade it by hand: change the image tags in its compose file, then run compose up -d.
detect.why_externalDb:
Its database is outside its compose project.
The installer only backs up the project's own database: upgrade it by hand.
detect.why_runnerLayout:
This Runner was not set up by the installer.
Upgrade it by hand, or install a new Runner with the installer and approve it in AnsibleForms.
detect.why_nativeLayout:
Its folder is not the installer's layout (releases/, current, app.env and rte.env).
Upgrade it by hand, the way it was installed.
detect.why_noHelm:
It runs on Kubernetes, but not as a release of the ansibleforms Helm chart (or helm is missing here).
Upgrade it with the tool that deployed it.
detect.why_unknownVersion:
Its version could not be read.
Start it so it answers on its port, then run the installer again.
detect.why_unmanaged:
AnsibleForms {version} answers on port {port}, but no engine manages it (run from source or by hand).
The installer cannot upgrade it. A new installation could clash with its ports or its database.
detect.why_unmanagedRunner:
An AnsibleForms RTE answers on port {port}, but no engine manages it (run from source or by hand).
The installer cannot upgrade it. A new installation could clash with its port.
kube.adoptValues: Saving the current values of {release} to {file}
